Record and transcribe on your Mac.
Straight answers to common Mac recording tasks, with the controls you need and no cloud workflow.
Can I screen record on my Mac or MacBook?

Yes. Open Luxel from the menu bar, choose a display, app window, or selected area, and start recording. The steps are the same on a MacBook Air or MacBook Pro, and you can add a camera overlay when you want to record yourself too.
How do I record my Mac screen with audio?
Choose what to capture, then turn on System Audio for app sound, Microphone for your voice, or both. Record, pause or resume as needed, then trim and export the finished video.
How do I transcribe a video or audio file to text?

Open a Luxel recording or another approved local media file, choose the spoken language, and create the transcript on your Mac. Search the text and jump to spoken words in the editor, or use the CLI to write text or JSON.
How do I record audio only on a Mac?
Choose a microphone and AAC or ALAC in Recording settings, then start Audio from the menu bar or use the Audio Only shortcut. Luxel saves an M4A file that you can play, transcribe, and export.
Choose the language spoken in your video or audio before you transcribe. Luxel processes the media on your Mac and writes the transcript in that same language.

Luxel records and edits the content you choose: screen video, system audio, microphone audio, camera preview overlays, replay buffer clips, transcripts, exports, settings, presets, history, and related caches. This processing happens on your Mac. Luxel does not upload this content to us.

Transcription uses local speech recognition. Optional speaker labeling uses model files included with Luxel and runs on your Mac. Luxel does not upload recordings for transcription or fall back to cloud transcription.

Optional Speech Detection Prompts are off by default. When you enable them, Luxel continuously analyzes short frames from the selected microphone on your Mac while the app is running and eligible. The detector looks for sustained speech-like sound; it does not identify meetings, calls, speakers, words, or meaning.
Detection frames are discarded unless you explicitly choose Start Recording. Before then, Luxel creates no pre-roll, media file, history item, transcript, sidecar, or cloud upload.

macOS may ask you to grant Screen & System Audio Recording, Microphone, Camera, Speech Recognition, file, folder, or automation permissions. Luxel uses those permissions only to perform the feature you request. We do not use permissions to build profiles, track behavior, or collect analytics.

If you opt in to Speech Detection Prompts, Luxel uses Microphone permission for ongoing local analysis while the app is running and eligible, and Notifications permission to show recording prompts. Turn the feature off at any time in Recording settings to stop that analysis.

Luxel does not sell personal information. Luxel does not share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising. Luxel does not track you across apps, websites, or services owned by other companies.

When Luxel detects a cue, the notification offers Start Recording and Dismiss. Start Recording begins one audio-only recording with the selected microphone. Dismiss does nothing, and opening the notification activates Luxel without recording.
Focus modes and other macOS notification settings may delay or hide the prompt. A prompt is a convenience, not a guarantee that Luxel recognizes a conversation.

While the feature is enabled, Luxel continuously analyzes short microphone frames on your Mac. Before you explicitly choose Start Recording, those frames are discarded and Luxel creates no pre-roll, media file, history item, transcript, sidecar, or cloud upload.
The detector looks only for sustained speech-like sound. It does not inspect app state or decide whether you are in a meeting or call.

Luxel pauses microphone analysis while a recording is active and while your Mac is locked or its display is asleep. Analysis resumes automatically when the recording ends or your Mac is awake and unlocked again.

Turn off Notify When Speech Is Detected to stop analysis and remove any outstanding prompt. If access was denied, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone and System Settings > Notifications > Luxel. Choose an available input in Recording settings, then turn the feature on again.

The notch controls are not visible
Luxel uses the built-in notch when a notched display is detected and the Notch setting is enabled. Otherwise it falls back to the floating HUD if that fallback is enabled, or to menu-bar-only status.
Enable Replay Buffer, grant Screen & System Audio Recording permission, and make sure a normal recording is not already active. Luxel pauses the buffer while regular recordings run.
Replay buffer clips are shorter than requested
The buffer can only export captured history that already exists. Wait until the menu reports that replay buffering is active before clipping the full selected duration.

Can I export audio in GIF or APNG?
No. GIF and APNG are animated image formats in Luxel and drop audio. Use MP4, HEVC MP4, ProRes MOV, WebM, or AV1 when audio is required.

Does Replay Buffer record all the time?
No. Replay Buffer is off until you enable it. While active, it is visible in the menu bar and can be stopped from the same controls.
